issues.detail: Error handling is mostly limited to brief notes (NET-0001 timeout, HTTP 429 backoff) with no code for handling failed requests, WebSocket errors or reconnects, and the Voice Agent API mentioned in the description is not actually covered with instructions or code.

scenarios.name: diarized-call-transcript-python
scenarios.rationale: B uses DeepgramClient with listen.v1.media.transcribe_file, nova-3, diarize=True, utterances=True, and loops over response.results.utterances printing speaker, start and transcript, so it covers the whole rubric. A calls the REST API with requests, never uses the SDK or utterances, and groups words by speaker by hand.

scenarios.name: voice-agent-turn-detection-flux
scenarios.rationale: B uses client.listen.v2.connect with flux-general-en, linear16, 16000, eot_threshold, eager_eot_threshold, the 50-70% LLM-call increase tied to TurnResumed, and no language parameter, while A uses a raw WebSocket instead of the SDK and never gives the 50-70% figure.

scenarios.name: live-captions-nodejs-keepalive
scenarios.rationale: Both use DeepgramClient and listen.v1.connect with the right options, handle Results and UtteranceEnd, and explain KeepAlive and NET-0001. B passes utterance_end_ms as a string as the rubric requires and states the 3-5 second interval, but its code has a few gaps. A sends utterance_end_ms as a number, which breaks the rubric's string requirement, but it sends CloseStream with Finalize and adds reconnect advice.
